service.name: Christmas jazz trio
service.serviceType: Christmas jazz trio for company holiday parties, December client dinners and private parties
service.description: A jazz trio playing the Christmas book, the Vince Guaraldi record and the standards of the season, on guitar, upright bass and drums with brushes, at conversation volume for company holiday parties, December client dinners and private parties across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain towns, with sound included.

faqs.q: Is a Christmas jazz trio too quiet for a holiday party?
faqs.a: For the dinner half, quiet is the job. With the drums played with brushes, the trio sits at the level of the conversation, so people at one table hear each other and still hear Linus and Lucy. Once the floor opens, the quartet with a singer plays the swing side of the book, or the DJ carries the rest of the night through the same sound system on the same contract.

faqs.q: How much space does it need?
faqs.a: One guitarist sets up in about 6 by 4 feet on one circuit, and the duo in a corner of about 8 by 6 feet. The trio takes about 12 by 8 feet on one dedicated circuit and needs about an hour to set up. Sound support that's the right size for the venue comes with every size.

faqs.q: How far ahead does a December date need to be booked?
faqs.a: Corporate holiday parties tend to get decided between August and October for November and December dates, and the peak Saturdays in December go first. Tell us the date and the venue, and we'll check the booking calendar and come back with a recommendation and a price for that night.

faqs.q: Does the Christmas jazz trio play New Year's Eve?
faqs.a: Yes. New Year's Eve gets booked earliest everywhere, and the set turns from carols to the standards and the swing book as the night goes on. Send the date early.

faqs.q: Can we ask for a particular song?
faqs.a: Yes. One learned song of your choosing comes with every booking, and you set the balance: carols all night, one Christmas set, or the mix the trio reads off the crowd.
